relevance_note: The review tabulates people who carry TNFAIP3 variants, including rows whose final diagnosis is 'A20 haploinsufficiency', so it describes identifiable individuals with TNFAIP3 variants.
method_note: Worked by reading the paper once and then writing this JSON by hand (no script was run); every span was copied from the Markdown. The paper is a review with no patients of its own: Tables 1-3 are literature tables of previously published people, each row with a per-patient reference column, which was copied into source_reference_in_review. Labels: no table has a patient label column and no row prints a patient number, so rule 3 applies, 'Table <n> row <k>' with k counting data rows from the top (Table 1 rows 1-6, Table 2 rows 1-46, Table 3 rows 1-14); the span given for such a label is the row's first cell (its mutation), which identifies the row. Table rows were filled only from their own row. The review's narrative paragraphs retell the same published cases but never give the mutation together with an identifiable person, so they were not mapped onto table rows and no rows were created for the narrative cases: doing so would require guessing which narrative person a table row is. Inheritance: the 'Family History' column states family history (Negative/Positive/De novo/Familial/NA), not the origin of the variant, so inheritance is 'not reported' for every row except the two where the text names a carrier parent for that person (Table 3 row 3, father carried the same variant; Table 3 row 10, mother also positive for the mutation). Variant type is recorded only where the paper states a class: Table 1 (large deletion/CNV, from the section and table titles 'Large deletions'), Table 3 (missense, from the title 'Missense mutations') and the two Table 2 rows whose Domain cell reads 'Splice site'; Table 2's title lists three classes ('splice site, frameshift, or nonsense') without saying which applies to which row, so the other Table 2 rows are 'not reported'. No table prints zygosity, a pathogenicity classification or ACMG criteria, so those are 'not reported' everywhere; the paper's bibliographic titles were not used for pathogenicity. functional_evidence_statement is filled only where the paper ties an assay to the exact variant string. Phenotypes: one row per symptom phrase printed in the row, all sharing the row's symptoms-cell span; no exclusions were recorded because no cell uses a symbol that the legend or text defines as absent (empty cells and 'NA' are not reported, and the text says only of Table 2 row 17 that no details 'were mentioned'). Stacked cells: no cell in these tables uses ' / '; cells printing two ages ('1.5 and 21 years', '28-61', '3 weeks-43 years', '9-41 years', '28-64', '1 months and 10 years', '6 months-28 years') were kept as one value and not split between people. Contradictions and oddities: the text calls Asp212Gly fs*38 'caused by a splice site mutation (c.634+2T>C)' although its row sits among frameshift variants, so its variant_type is 'not reported'; Table 2 row 33 prints 'Ala434Ter (c.1300_1301 delinsTA)' while the text prints 'p.Ala434Ter (c.1300_1301delinsTA)'; Table 3 row 13 prints the domain as 'ZNFf4', recorded verbatim; the text says of Phe224Ser fs*4 that 'One of the patients also developed retinal vasculitis' without naming which patient; references [30], [31], [32], [34], [38], [48], [49] and [65] are each cited for several different people, so a reference alone does not identify a person. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients is null because the review has no patients of its own and does not say that any patient of its own was described earlier; n_patients_reported and cohort_size_as_stated are null because the authors give no total. phenotype_checklist gives one row per individual and checklist feature (20 rows per person), 1320 rows in all; each status follows that individual's phenotypic_features rows. The checklist_feature names come from the schema and carry no span; for compactness the checklist rows for 'observed' items are recorded without their own span, and the supporting quote is the matching phenotypic_features row of the same person (the first six checklist blocks, for Table 1 rows 1-6, do carry that span).
